# Hypothesis Testing {.hero #s06-testing}

::: {.sem-mark data-sem="6"}
Tests for one and two population means
:::

## Testing the effect of a marketing campaign {.formula-slide .example #web-test}

::: {.lede-min}
A website averaged $\mu = 10{,}372$ visits a day. After a marketing campaign, 30 days give a sample mean $\bar x = 10{,}628$, with sample SD 402. Did the campaign work?
:::

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.fragment}
[Two explanations]{.col-head}
[Null and alternative hypotheses]{.col-sub}

**A. $H_0$:** the mean has not changed, $\mu = 10{,}372$; the rise is chance.

**B. $H_1$:** the mean has increased, $\mu > 10{,}372$; the rise is too large to be random.

:::

::: {.fragment}
[Procedure]{.col-head}
[Calculating the test statistic and p-value]{.col-sub}

**I.** Assume $H_0$ is true: the average is still $10{,}372$.

**II.** Count the standard errors between $\bar x$ and $\mu_0$:

$$z = \frac{\bar x - \mu_0}{s/\sqrt n} = \frac{10{,}628 - 10{,}372}{402/\sqrt{30}} \approx 3.49$$

**III.** The p-value: $p = P(Z \ge 3.49) = 0.0002$, the chance of a $z$ this large if $H_0$ were true.

**IV.** Choose $\alpha = 0.05$ beforehand: reject $H_0$ when $z \ge z_{0.05} = 1.645$, the same as $p < 0.05$. Here $3.49 \ge 1.645$: **reject $H_0$**.
:::
::::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
402 is a sample SD, so strictly this is the $t$ case of the next slides: $t = 3.49$ on 29 df gives $p \approx 0.0008$. The conclusion is unchanged.
:::

## Four Steps of a Test {.qcard-slide #test-steps}

::: {.lede-min}
A test compares the sample mean $\bar x$ with a hypothesised population mean $\mu_0$, allowing for sampling variation. Use the following four steps.
:::

:::: {.prop-grid}

::: {.prop-card .prop-hyp .fragment}
[Hypotheses]{.prop-name}

[$H_0\!: \mu = \mu_0$]{.prop-math}

[State the null hypothesis and the alternative $H_1$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-stat .fragment}
[Statistic]{.prop-name}

[$z = \dfrac{\bar x - \mu_0}{\sigma / \sqrt n}$]{.prop-math}

[How many standard errors $\bar x$ lies from $\mu_0$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-crit .fragment}
[Critical Value]{.prop-name}

[$z > z_\alpha$]{.prop-math}

[Reject $H_0$ if the statistic lands past the cut-off.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-pval .fragment}
[P-Value]{.prop-name}

[$p < \alpha$]{.prop-math}

[Or reject if the tail area beyond it is below $\alpha$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
The last two always agree: the statistic is past the cut-off exactly when the area beyond it is below $\alpha$.
:::

## The z and t Test Statistics {.formula-slide #test-stats}

::: {.lede-min}
Both count standard errors between $\bar x$ and $\mu_0$; the choice of table depends on whether $\sigma$ is known.
:::

$$\textstyle Z = \frac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\color{#325D88}{\sigma} / \sqrt n} \sim N(0, 1) \;\; \color{#6E7681}{\sigma \text{ known}} \qquad\quad T = \frac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\color{#B94A48}{S} / \sqrt n} \sim t_{n-1} \;\; \color{#6E7681}{\sigma \text{ unknown}}$$

::: {.deriv-arrow .fragment}
[↓]{.deriv-glyph} [The alternative $H_1$ decides which tail or tails to use]{.deriv-note}
:::

::: {.h1-table .fragment}
| Alternative $H_1$ | Reject $H_0$ if | P-value |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| $\mu > \mu_0$ | $z > z_\alpha$ | $p = P(Z > z)$ |
| $\mu < \mu_0$ | $z < -z_\alpha$ | $p = P(Z < z)$ |
| $\mu \neq \mu_0$ | $\lvert z \rvert > z_{\alpha/2}$ | $p = 2P(Z > \lvert z \rvert)$ |
:::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
With $t$, use $t_\alpha$ on $n - 1$ degrees of freedom. Its critical values are larger in magnitude, so the same statistic can reject $H_0$ in a $z$ test and fail to reject it in a $t$ test.
:::

## Comparing the sample with the null hypothesis {.stage-slide #pval-intuition}

::: {.lede-min}
Test $H_0\!: \mu = \mu_0$ against $H_1\!: \mu > \mu_0$. Our sample gave $z = 2.0$. Is that surprising if $H_0$ is true?
:::

::: {.stage-wrap .stage-wrap-std}
<div id="pval-stage" class="stage"></div>
:::

[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="pval-frag-3" data-fragment-index="3"}

:::: {.pv-read .fragment data-fragment-index="4"}
::: {}
[Tail probability]{.pv-head}
If $H_0$ were true, a $z$ at least as large as ours would come up less than 5% of the time. That is rare enough to reject $H_0$.
:::

::: {}
[Repeated experiments]{.pv-head}
If $H_0$ is true and I repeat the experiment, chance alone produces a result at least this extreme only $p$% of the time: here about 2.3%.
:::
::::

## Rejection Region and P-Value {.ojs-slide .example #reject-lab}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Defaults are Exercise 1 of the beamer Seminar 5: z = 2.5, right-tailed, 5%.
viewof rjIn = Inputs.form({
  test: Inputs.radio(["Normal z", "Student's t"], {value: "Normal z", label: "Test"}),
  df: Inputs.range([1, 60], {value: 24, step: 1, label: "Degrees of freedom"}),
  tail: Inputs.radio(["Left", "Right", "Two-tailed"], {value: "Right", label: "Tail"}),
  alpha: Inputs.range([0.01, 0.1], {value: 0.05, step: 0.005, label: html`Significance <i style="text-transform: none">α</i>`}),
  stat: Inputs.range([-4, 4], {value: 2.5, step: 0.01, label: "Observed statistic"})
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="rj-dials">${ins.test}${ins.df}${ins.tail}</div><div class="rj-dials">${ins.alpha}${ins.stat}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// The t density from the same log-gamma as clTcdf (section 05), so the curve,
// the cut-off and the p-value all come from one distribution.
rjTdens = (x, df) => Math.exp(clLgam((df + 1) / 2) - clLgam(df / 2) - 0.5 * Math.log(df * Math.PI)
  - (df + 1) / 2 * Math.log(1 + x * x / df))
rjDens = x => Math.exp(-0.5 * x * x) / Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI)
// Cut-off c (positive), p-value and decision for one test; cdf is its CDF.
rjRule = (cdf, tail, a, s) => {
  const c = clInv(cdf)(1 - (tail === "Two-tailed" ? a / 2 : a));
  const p = tail === "Right" ? 1 - cdf(s) : tail === "Left" ? cdf(s) : 2 * (1 - cdf(Math.abs(s)));
  const rej = tail === "Right" ? s > c : tail === "Left" ? s < -c : Math.abs(s) > c;
  return {c, p, rej};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const isT = rjIn.test === "Student's t", df = rjIn.df, {tail, alpha, stat} = rjIn;
  const cdf = isT ? (x => clTcdf(x, df)) : Phi, dens = isT ? (x => rjTdens(x, df)) : rjDens;
  const {c, p, rej} = rjRule(cdf, tail, alpha, stat);
  const sym = isT ? "t" : "z", lo = -4.5, hi = 4.5, s = Math.abs(stat);
  const grid = d3.range(0, 401).map(i => lo + (hi - lo) * i / 400);
  const reg = {Right: [[c, hi]], Left: [[lo, -c]], "Two-tailed": [[lo, -c], [c, hi]]}[tail];
  const pv = {Right: [[stat, hi]], Left: [[lo, stat]], "Two-tailed": [[lo, -s], [s, hi]]}[tail];
  const cuts = reg.map(([u, v]) => u === lo ? v : u);
  const top = rjDens(0), f = (v, k = 3) => v.toFixed(k).replace("-", "−");   // a true minus sign
  const area = (pieces, fill, op) => pieces.map(([u, v]) => Plot.areaY(grid.filter(x => x >= u && x <= v),
    {x: d => d, y: dens, fill, fillOpacity: op}));
  const halo = {stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6};
  const plot = Plot.plot({
    width: 920, height: 270, marginLeft: 20, marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 34,
    style: ({fontSize: "15px", fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif", color: PPAL.soft, background: "transparent"}),
    x: {domain: [lo, hi], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0, top * 1.02], axis: null},
    marks: [
      ...area(reg, PPAL.brick, 0.3),
      ...area(pv, PPAL.orange, 0.45),
      Plot.line(grid, {x: d => d, y: dens, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.ruleX(cuts, {y1: 0, y2: top * 0.6, stroke: PPAL.brick, strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      Plot.text(cuts, {x: d => d, y: top * 0.6, dy: -10, text: d => f(d), fill: PPAL.brick, fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 700, ...halo}),
      Plot.ruleX([stat], {y1: 0, y2: top * 0.88, stroke: PPAL.orange, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.text([stat], {x: d => d, y: top * 0.88, dy: -10, text: d => `${sym} = ${f(d, 2)}`, fill: PPAL.orange, fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 700, ...halo}),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: PPAL.dim}),
      Plot.text([isT ? `Null distribution: t with ${df} degrees of freedom` : "Null distribution: N(0, 1)"],
        {frameAnchor: "top-left", dy: -28, text: d => d, fill: PPAL.navy, fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 16, ...halo})
    ]
  });
  // Exercise 5: on t, say what z would have decided with the same statistic.
  const z = rjRule(Phi, tail, alpha, stat);
  const cs = v => tail === "Two-tailed" ? `±${f(v)}` : f(tail === "Left" ? -v : v);
  const alt = isT && z.rej !== rej
    ? ` With z the cut-off would be ${cs(z.c)} and we would ${z.rej ? "reject" : "fail to reject"}: the heavier t tails give a larger critical value.` : "";
  const msg = `The statistic ${sym} = ${f(stat, 2)} is ${rej ? "inside" : "outside"} the rejection region (cut-off ${cs(c)}), and its p-value ${f(p, 4)} is ${p < alpha ? "below" : "above"} α = ${+alpha.toFixed(3)}: <b>${rej ? "reject" : "fail to reject"} H₀</b>.${alt}`;
  return html`${plot}
  <div class="ojs-eq cl-stats">
    <span>Critical value = <span class="miss">${cs(c)}</span></span>
    <span>P-value = <span class="rate">${f(p, 4)}</span></span>
    <span>Decision: ${rej ? "Reject H₀" : "Fail to reject H₀"}</span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${msg}</div>`;
}
```

## Four Outcomes of a Test {.formula-slide #err-table}

::: {.lede-min}
Combining the two test decisions with whether $H_0$ is true gives four possible outcomes. Two are correct decisions and two are errors.
:::

::: {.fragment}
```{=html}
<table class="err-table" data-quarto-disable-processing="true">
  <colgroup><col style="width:56px"><col style="width:190px"><col style="width:290px"><col style="width:290px"></colgroup>
  <thead>
    <tr><th class="w-side"></th><th class="w-row"></th><th colspan="2" class="err-top w-cells">Actual truth</th></tr>
    <tr><th></th><th></th><th>H₀ is true</th><th>H₀ is false</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th rowspan="2" class="err-side"><span>Decision</span></th><th>Reject H₀</th>
        <td class="err-bad"><b>Type I error</b><br>probability <i>α</i> (5%)</td>
        <td class="err-ok"><b>Correct</b><br>probability 1 − <i>β</i>, the <b>power</b></td></tr>
    <tr><th>Fail to reject H₀</th>
        <td class="err-ok"><b>Correct</b><br>probability 1 − <i>α</i></td>
        <td class="err-bad"><b>Type II error</b><br>probability <i>β</i></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
$\alpha$ is the **significance level**, chosen before looking at the data; $1 - \beta$ is the **power**, the probability of detecting a real change. The next slide shows how $n$ and $\alpha$ trade them off.
:::

## Type I and Type II Errors {.ojs-slide .example #power-lab}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Exercise 1 of the beamer Seminar 5: H0: mu = 1300 against mu > 1300,
// sigma = 720, n = 36. The true mean defaults to the observed 1600.
pwMu0 = 1300
pwSd = 720
viewof pwIn = Inputs.form({
  mu: Inputs.range([1300, 1900], {value: 1600, step: 10, label: html`True mean <i style="text-transform: none">μ</i>`}),
  n: Inputs.range([9, 144], {value: 36, step: 1, label: html`Sample size <i style="text-transform: none">n</i>`}),
  alpha: Inputs.range([0.01, 0.1], {value: 0.05, step: 0.005, label: html`Significance <i style="text-transform: none">α</i>`})
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="rj-dials">${Object.values(ins)}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {mu, n, alpha} = pwIn, se = pwSd / Math.sqrt(n);
  const c = pwMu0 + clInv(Phi)(1 - alpha) * se;          // reject H0 when the sample mean exceeds c
  const beta = Phi((c - mu) / se), power = 1 - beta;
  const lo = pwMu0 - 4 * se, hi = Math.max(mu, pwMu0) + 4 * se;
  const grid = d3.range(0, 401).map(i => lo + (hi - lo) * i / 400);
  const dn = m => x => Math.exp(-0.5 * ((x - m) / se) ** 2) / (se * Math.sqrt(2 * Math.PI));
  const d0 = dn(pwMu0), d1 = dn(mu), top = d0(pwMu0), same = mu === pwMu0;
  const halo = {stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6};
  const f = (v, k = 1) => v.toFixed(k), pc = v => `${f(100 * v)}%`;
  const plot = Plot.plot({
    width: 1000, height: 300, marginLeft: 20, marginRight: 20, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 40,
    style: ({fontSize: "15px", fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif", color: PPAL.soft, background: "transparent"}),
    x: {domain: [lo, hi], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0, top * 1.15], axis: null, insetTop: 12},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(grid.filter(x => x <= c), {x: d => d, y: d1, fill: PPAL.orange, fillOpacity: same ? 0 : 0.4}),
      Plot.areaY(grid.filter(x => x >= c), {x: d => d, y: d0, fill: PPAL.brick, fillOpacity: 0.45}),
      Plot.line(grid, {x: d => d, y: d1, stroke: PPAL.olive, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.line(grid, {x: d => d, y: d0, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 2.5, strokeDasharray: same ? "6 4" : null}),
      Plot.ruleX([c], {y1: 0, y2: top * 1.05, stroke: "#3E3F3A", strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      Plot.text([c], {x: d => d, y: top * 0.55, dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", text: d => `Cut-off ${f(d)}`, fill: "#3E3F3A", fontSize: 15, ...halo}),
      Plot.text([pwMu0], {x: d => d, y: top, dy: -10, text: d => `H₀: μ = ${d}`, fill: PPAL.navy, fontSize: 15, fontWeight: 700, ...halo}),
      ...(same ? [] : [Plot.text([mu], {x: d => d, y: top, dy: -10, text: d => `True μ = ${d}`, fill: PPAL.olive, fontSize: 15, fontWeight: 700, ...halo})]),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: PPAL.dim}),
      Plot.text([`Sample means under H₀ and under the true mean, σ/√n = ${f(se)}`],
        {frameAnchor: "top-left", dy: -28, text: d => d, fill: PPAL.navy, fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 16, ...halo})
    ]
  });
  const msg = same
    ? `The true mean is μ₀, so H₀ holds and the only possible mistake is a <b>Type I error</b>: rejecting it anyway, ${pc(alpha)} of the time.`
    : `If the true mean is ${mu}, a sample of ${n} days lands past the cut-off with probability <b>${pc(power)}</b>, the power. It misses ${pc(beta)} of the time, a <b>Type II error</b>. A larger n shrinks β; a smaller α cuts false alarms but widens β.`;
  return html`${plot}
  <div class="ojs-eq cl-stats">
    <span>Type I: <span class="miss">α = ${pc(alpha)}</span></span>
    <span>Type II: <span class="rate">${same ? "None, H₀ is true" : `β = ${pc(beta)}`}</span></span>
    <span>Power = <span class="hit">${same ? "n/a" : pc(power)}</span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${msg}</div>`;
}
```

## Three Ways to Compare Two Means {.qcard-slide #two-mean-tests}

::: {.lede-min}
Each test divides the gap between two sample means by its standard error. How the data were collected decides which standard error to use.
:::

:::: {.prop-grid}

::: {.prop-card .prop-pooled .fragment}
[Pooled t]{.prop-name}

[$t = \dfrac{\bar x_1 - \bar x_2}{\sqrt{s_p^2\big(\tfrac{1}{n_1} + \tfrac{1}{n_2}\big)}}$]{.prop-math}

[Independent samples, normal, equal variances. Compare with $t_{n_1 + n_2 - 2}$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-welch .fragment}
[Large samples]{.prop-name}

[$z = \dfrac{\bar x_1 - \bar x_2}{\sqrt{\frac{s_1^2}{n_1} + \frac{s_2^2}{n_2}}}$]{.prop-math}

[Independent samples, unequal variances, large $n$. Compare with $N(0, 1)$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-paired .fragment}
[Paired t]{.prop-name}

[$t = \dfrac{\bar d}{s_d / \sqrt{n}}$]{.prop-math}

[The same units measured twice. Test the differences $d$ against $t_{n - 1}$.]{.prop-q}
:::

::::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
The next slide builds the pooled test and its interval; the two after it show why paired data must not be treated as independent.
:::

## Pooling the Two Variances {.formula-slide #pooled-formula}

::: {.lede-min}
Both samples estimate one shared $\sigma^2$, so we pool them, weighted by degrees of freedom.
:::

$$\textstyle s_p^2 \;=\; \frac{(n_1 - 1)\,s_1^2 \;+\; (n_2 - 1)\,s_2^2}{n_1 + n_2 - 2}$$

::: {.deriv-arrow .fragment}
[↓]{.deriv-glyph} [Put $s_p^2$ in place of $\sigma^2$ in the standard error of $\bar x_1 - \bar x_2$]{.deriv-note}
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\textstyle T \;=\; \frac{(\bar X_1 - \bar X_2) \,-\, (\mu_1 - \mu_2)}{\sqrt{S_p^2\big(\tfrac{1}{n_1} + \tfrac{1}{n_2}\big)}} \;\sim\; \color{#325D88}{t_{\,n_1 + n_2 - 2}}$$
:::

::: {.deriv-arrow .fragment}
[↓]{.deriv-glyph} [Rearrange the test inequality to obtain a confidence interval]{.deriv-note}
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\textstyle \mu_1 - \mu_2 \;\in\; (\bar x_1 - \bar x_2) \;\pm\; \color{#B94A48}{t_{\alpha/2,\; n_1 + n_2 - 2}}\, \sqrt{s_p^2\big(\tfrac{1}{n_1} + \tfrac{1}{n_2}\big)}$$
:::

## Repeated measurements on the same firms {.stage-slide #pair-intuition}

::: {.lede-min}
The cost of equity (%) of the same 15 firms, before and after 2020. Did it fall?
:::

::: {.stage-wrap .stage-wrap-std}
<div id="pair-stage" class="stage"></div>
:::

[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="pair-frag-1" data-fragment-index="1"}
[]{.fragment .fi-frag id="pair-frag-2" data-fragment-index="2"}

::: {.slide-footer .fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
Variation in cost of equity between firms can obscure the change between periods. Calculating each firm's difference removes its initial level, allowing each firm to act as its own control.
:::

## Paired and independent samples tests {.ojs-slide .example #pair-lab}

::: {.lede-min}
$H_0$: the mean change is 0. $H_1$: the cost of equity fell (left-tailed). Same data, two tests.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof plIn = Inputs.form({
  mode: Inputs.radio(["Paired", "Independent"], {value: "Paired", label: "Treat the data as"}),
  alpha: Inputs.radio(["α = 1%", "α = 5%"], {value: "α = 1%", label: "Significance level"})
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="cl-dials pl-dials">${ins.mode}${ins.alpha}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Table 1 of beamer Seminar 6, Exercise 3: cost of equity (%) of 15 firms.
plPre  = [3, 5, 4, 1, 4, 8, 10, 15, 2, 9, 6, 3, 8, 11, 10]
plPost = [1, 6, 3, 2, 7, 3, 5, 8, 4, 7, 4, 2, 5, 7, 5]
plDif  = plPost.map((v, i) => v - plPre[i])
// H1: the cost fell, so both tests are left-tailed. The density reuses
// clLgam and the CDF clTcdf, both from #ci-lab.
plTpdf = (t, df) => Math.exp(clLgam((df + 1) / 2) - clLgam(df / 2) - 0.5 * Math.log(df * Math.PI)
  - (df + 1) / 2 * Math.log(1 + t * t / df))
plTests = {
  const n = plPre.length, est = d3.mean(plDif);
  const vPre = d3.variance(plPre), vPost = d3.variance(plPost), vDif = d3.variance(plDif);
  const sp2 = ((n - 1) * vPre + (n - 1) * vPost) / (2 * n - 2);
  const mk = (se, df) => ({se, df, t: est / se, p: clTcdf(est / se, df)});
  return {n, est, vPre, vPost, vDif,
    Paired: mk(Math.sqrt(vDif / n), n - 1),
    Independent: mk(Math.sqrt(sp2 * 2 / n), 2 * n - 2)};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const T = plTests, paired = plIn.mode === "Paired", cur = T[plIn.mode];
  const a = plIn.alpha === "α = 1%" ? 0.01 : 0.05, crit = -clInv(t => clTcdf(t, cur.df))(1 - a);
  const style = ({fontSize: "14px", fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif", color: PPAL.soft, background: "transparent"});
  const title = s => Plot.text([s], {frameAnchor: "top-left", dy: -30, text: d => d, fill: PPAL.navy, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6, fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 16});
  const neg = s => s.replace("-", "−");
  // Ties fan out sideways so no dot hides another: pre to the left and post to
  // the right, away from the joining lines, which all run edge to edge.
  const jit = (vals, side) => { const seen = {}; return vals.map(v => { const j = (seen[v] = (seen[v] || 0) + 1) - 1;
    return (side ? side * j : (j % 2 ? -1 : 1) * Math.ceil(j / 2)) * 0.09; }); };
  const jPre = jit(plPre, -1), jPost = jit(plPost, 1), jDif = jit(plDif, 0);
  const idx = d3.range(T.n), XD = 2.3;
  const names = new Map([[0, "Pre 2020"], [1, "Post 2020"], [XD, "Post − pre"]]);
  const data = Plot.plot({
    width: 470, height: 290, marginLeft: 34, marginBottom: 30, marginTop: 42, style,
    x: {domain: [-0.5, XD + 0.6], ticks: [0, 1, XD], tickFormat: v => names.get(v), label: null, tickSize: 0},
    y: {domain: [-8, 16], ticks: [-8, -4, 0, 4, 8, 12, 16], tickFormat: v => neg(String(v)), label: null, insetTop: 18},
    marks: [
      title(`The ${T.n} firms, pre and post 2020`),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {x1: XD - 0.5, x2: XD + 0.5, stroke: PPAL.soft, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      paired ? Plot.link(idx, {x1: 0.06, y1: i => plPre[i], x2: 0.94, y2: i => plPost[i], stroke: PPAL.dim, strokeWidth: 1.2}) : null,
      Plot.dot(idx, {x: i => jPre[i], y: i => plPre[i], r: 5, fill: PPAL.navy, fillOpacity: 0.6}),
      Plot.dot(idx, {x: i => 1 + jPost[i], y: i => plPost[i], r: 5, fill: PPAL.olive, fillOpacity: 0.7}),
      Plot.ruleY([d3.mean(plPre)], {x1: -0.3, x2: 0.3, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.ruleY([d3.mean(plPost)], {x1: 0.7, x2: 1.3, stroke: PPAL.olive, strokeWidth: 3}),
      paired ? Plot.dot(idx, {x: i => XD + jDif[i], y: i => plDif[i], r: 5, fill: PPAL.orange, fillOpacity: 0.7}) : null,
      Plot.ruleY([T.est], {x1: XD - 0.3, x2: XD + 0.3, stroke: PPAL.orange, strokeWidth: 3})
    ]
  });
  const G = d3.range(-4.5, 4.501, 0.05), tail = G.filter(t => t <= crit);
  const dist = Plot.plot({
    width: 470, height: 290, marginLeft: 12, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 30, marginTop: 42, style,
    x: {domain: [-4.5, 4.5], label: null, tickSize: 4, tickFormat: v => neg(String(v))},
    y: {domain: [0, 0.42], axis: null, insetTop: 18},
    marks: [
      title(`The statistic against t with ${cur.df} df`),
      Plot.areaY(tail, {x: t => t, y: t => plTpdf(t, cur.df), fill: PPAL.brick, fillOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.lineY(G, {x: t => t, y: t => plTpdf(t, cur.df), stroke: PPAL.soft, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: PPAL.dim}),
      Plot.ruleX([crit], {y1: 0, y2: 0.3, stroke: PPAL.brick, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      Plot.ruleX([cur.t], {y1: 0, y2: 0.36, stroke: "#3E3F3A", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.text([cur.t], {x: t => t, y: 0.36, dy: -10, dx: -12, textAnchor: "start", text: t => `t = ${neg(t.toFixed(3))}`,
        fill: "#3E3F3A", stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6, fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 700})
    ]
  });
  const m = v => neg(v.toFixed(3)), f4 = v => v.toFixed(4);
  const row = k => html`<span class="${k === plIn.mode ? "pl-on" : "pl-off"}">${k}: SE = ${m(T[k].se)}, t = ${m(T[k].t)}, p = ${f4(T[k].p)}</span>`;
  const rej = cur.p < a;
  const why = paired
    ? `Firms that start high stay high, so the differences vary far less than the two groups together: variance <b>${T.vDif.toFixed(2)}</b> against ${(T.vPre + T.vPost).toFixed(2)}.`
    : `Treated as independent, the firm-to-firm spread stays in the standard error: <b>${m(T.Independent.se)}</b> instead of ${m(T.Paired.se)}.`;
  return html`<div class="cr-row pl-row">${data}${dist}</div>
  <div class="ojs-eq cl-stats pl-stats">${row("Paired")}${row("Independent")}</div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">p = ${f4(cur.p)} is ${rej ? "below" : "above"} ${plIn.alpha.replace("α = ", "")}, so we <b>${rej ? "reject" : "do not reject"} H<sub>0</sub></b>. ${why}</div>`;
}
```
